_about: Provenance of the 17 sages added with the owner's tier-A Shem HaGedolim research papers (ids 680-696), generated from the validated fragments. Same shape as shem-hagedolim-additions.json, plus `claims`: for every sentence of the Hebrew, English and Russian bio and core idea, the verbatim source quotes it rests on. Per sage: the Maarekhet Sefarim/Gedolim entry that names him (shg), the sources read, the links with their quotes, and the worker's notes. Never hand-edit; tests/shemHagedolim2.test.ts fails when an id now belongs to another sage.

sages.notes: Sources: the owner's paper (680) is the primary and only biographical source. The Hebrew Wikipedia article and the Sefaria topic page could not be fetched in this session (WebFetch returned URL_NOT_FOUND for every he.wikipedia title tried, hamichlol is robots-blocked, and Sefaria's topic API returned an empty object for yehudai-gaon). The English Wikipedia article (as extracted by WebFetch, short quotes only, saved in enwiki.txt) agrees on the tenure, "head of the yeshiva in Sura from 757 to 761", and gives no birth or death year, no mention of blindness or of his brother; the paper itself cites he.wikipedia (Halachot Pesukot), Oxford Reference and Danzig's introduction. Maarekhet: Shem HaGedolim, Maarekhet Sefarim has no entry for him; under Letter He 64 (Halachot Pesukot) the Chida writes "(ע' רב יהודאי גאון בח"א)", a cross-reference to his own entry for Rav Yehudai Gaon in Maarekhet Gedolim, Chet Alef (that part of the book is not on Sefaria, so the entry itself was not read). Other Maarekhet Sefarim entries that name him, read but not used: He 61 (Halachot Gedolot: "מיחסים אותו בכמה דוכתי לרבינו יהודאי גאון", the authorship of Halachot Gedolot is disputed) and Bet 129 (Basar al gabei gechalim: the Rokeach writes that Rav Yehudai Gaon composed it). Years: the paper gives only his term as head of the Sura yeshiva, 757-761 CE (written ד'תקי"ז-ד'תקכ"א), no birth or death year, and 762 for the founding of Baghdad. Giving 757-761 as era would have made the rebuild store a four-year "life"; so era is the century (המאה ה־8), date_precision century, and the term of office appears only in the bio. Left out: the account ("according to historical traditions") of his and his brother Dudai's part in blocking Anan ben David's candidacy as exilarch (a tradition the paper itself hedges); the takkanah of the moredet and the claim that he took part in it; the "Halachot Ra'u" Hebrew translation details; the claim that Halachot Gedolot was written about half a century later (the paper states it as research, Halachot Gedolot is the work of R. Shimon Kayyara; not needed for the record); Rashi as one who "cited" him (no influence link made for Rashi: a citation is not stated as an influence in a form worth a link). Judgement calls: "Halachot Pesukot" is the paper's "composed by him, or in his study house under his direct inspiration", kept as such, and "first codification attempt" is the paper's statement, kept in the paper's words as a statement about the book. The influence link to the Rif (582) rests on the paper's sentence that the Rif's main work "continues in large part his way"; direction source=influencer. Not linked, because not on the roster: his brother Rav Dudai Gaon, his student Rav Abba (Halachot de-Rav Abba), Pirkoi ben Baboi, Anan ben David, Rav Shimon Kayyara, Rav Hai Gaon is on the roster (25) but the paper only says Rav Hai noted the difficulty of attributing traditions to him centuries later (not a teacher/student/influence statement). SECOND READING (Q1): full hewiki/enwiki texts now saved and used; all sentences checked against paper and wiki: correct. Hewiki states that only 'some scholars' attribute Halachot Pesukot to him (the sentence keeps the paper's 'by him or in his study house'). Hewiki also names Natronai bar Hachinai as his student (not on roster). Roster candidates checked, no further link stated: Rav Hai (25), Rav Saadia (344), Rav Sherira (21).

sages.notes: Sources: the owner's paper (681) is the only biographical source. The Hebrew Wikipedia article (the paper itself rests on he.wikipedia, "רב (אמורא)") and Sefaria's topic page could not be fetched in this session (WebFetch: URL_NOT_FOUND for he.wikipedia, empty answers from the Sefaria topic API). The English Wikipedia article "Abba Arikha" was reached, but WebFetch gives only short extracted quotes (saved in enwiki.txt): it confirms "amora of the 3rd century", 175–247 CE and the year 219; it did not give a sentence on "halakha follows Rav in prohibitions" or on the Rosh Hashanah liturgy, so those two core-idea sentences rest on the paper alone. Maarekhet: shg is null. Shem HaGedolim, Maarekhet Sefarim (the only part on Sefaria) has no entry for him or for a book of his; I searched all 22 letters for "אבא אריכא", "דבי רב" and for entries naming him. The closest are Samekh 52 (Sifra: "הוא תורת כהנים והרמב"ם כתב בהקדמתו שרב חיברו", i.e. the Chida reports the Rambam's view that Rav composed the Sifra, which the same entry then disputes) and Samekh 62 (Sifrei de-Vei Rav, a commentary entry that does not name him). Neither is an entry about Rav, so neither is used as shg; the Samekh 52 line is saved in maarekhet.txt for the lead's decision. His own entry is in Maarekhet Gedolim (not on Sefaria). Years: the paper gives no birth or death year, only that he returned to Babylonia around 219 CE (en.wikipedia, as extracted: "the 219th year of the Common Era") and the Sassanid rise in 226. The years 175–247 come from the English Wikipedia lead as WebFetch extracted it ("Rav Abba bar Aybo ... 175–247 CE), commonly known as Abba Arikha"); I could not read the article's full text or he.wikipedia to see whether it marks them approximate, so era is written כ־175–247 (the roster's sign for approximate dates) and the owner's paper, which names no year, neither confirms nor contradicts them. Left out (doubtful, disputed or not about him as a person): the claim that some Rishonim held Rav edited the Sifra and Sifrei, which the paper itself says Rashi disputes; the page's statements that Sura "continued almost eight hundred years" (a statement about the institution), the lists of his takkanot (lashes for betrothal in the market, no betrothal of a minor daughter) and of his aggadic sayings, the explanation of the name Abba Arikha (the paper gives several), the claim that he held the world was created in Tishrei, the descriptions of his students' institutions beyond the three named; the family lineage to King David (tradition). Judgement calls: the partial ordination sentence ("יורה יורה" only) is the paper's, from Wikipedia as it cites; the rule "halakha follows Rav in prohibitions and Shmuel in monetary law" is stated in the paper as a rule with Abaye's exceptions left out. Links: teacher Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi (580) "רבו"; Rabbi Chiya (7) is his uncle (family, elder first); students Rav Huna (576), Rav Chisda (536) named as his students, and Rav Yehuda (522): the paper says only "רב יהודה … שלמד אצל רב ואחר כך אצל שמואל" and that he founded the Pumbedita yeshiva, which is Rav Yehuda bar Yechezkel on the roster (location פומבדיתא), identification by that description; Shmuel (482) is called "ידידו בר הפלוגתא" (colleague). Rav Chisda's label says 217-309, Rav Huna 216-296, as the roster has them. Validator: ru.label "Рав (Абба Арика)" collides with the dead overlay key sup-84 (en "Rav (Abba Arika)"), a key CLAUDE.md says is ignored; the label is the binding table's, so it is kept and the error is expected until the validator or the dead key is dealt with. SECOND READING (Q1): hewiki/enwiki full texts saved. Fixes: (1) core s1 scope: the rule governs the disputes of Rav and Shmuel (hewiki, Bechorot 49b; paper 'להכריע במאות המחלוקות ביניהם'), not all prohibition law, and Abaye lists three exceptions; (2) bio s2: the sources disagree on the occasion of the ordination (paper: when he asked to return; hewiki: Rabbi Chiya asked Rabbi to ordain Rav and Rabba bar Chana), so the occasion is dropped; the limits are the paper's and hewiki's common point (no permission for a blemished firstborn); the paper adds no 'ידין ידין' (not stated); (3) bio s3: hewiki and enwiki say Rav first worked in Nehardea (market-master, lecturer for Rav Shela) and went to Sura later, so 'on his return he founded Sura' became 'returned c. 219, later founded his yeshiva in Sura'. 'Yarchei Kallah' rests on the paper alone (neither wiki has it). Aleinu: enwiki says some attribute authorship or revision to Rav; the sentence says only that it was incorporated in the arrangement credited to him. Years כ־175–247: hewiki 175 (לערך) – 247, enwiki 175–247. Added teacher link Chiya->Rav (hewiki: studied under his uncle R. Chiya; the family link stays). SHG: the Chida's Sifra entry (Samekh 52:1) reports the Rambam's view that Rav composed the Sifra and the Karban Aharon's doubt; used as shg because it names Rav and a book attributed to him, with that caveat; his own entry is in Maarekhet Gedolim (not on Sefaria).

sages.notes: Sources: the owner's paper (682) is the only biographical source. The Hebrew Wikipedia article and Sefaria's topic page could not be fetched in this session (WebFetch: URL_NOT_FOUND for he.wikipedia, empty answers from the Sefaria topic API). The English Wikipedia article was reached, but WebFetch gives only short extracted quotes (saved in enwiki.txt); it agrees on birth in Salamanca in 1452, the Chibbur completed in 1478 in Hebrew in Salamanca, royal astronomer to King John II, flight to Tunis and a probable death in 1515 in Jerusalem, and it differs from the paper in two things (below); the paper itself cites en.wikipedia (Abraham Zacuto), a Kiddle copy of it, iyun.org.il, a Jewish Virtual Library Facebook post, he.wikisource (Sefer Yuchasin) and a University of Washington article. Maarekhet: the Chida's own entry for him is in Maarekhet Gedolim (not on Sefaria). In Maarekhet Sefarim (all 22 letters scanned for "אברהם זכות", "זקות" and "יוחסין") he is named only by his book, as "הרב ספר יוחסין": Ayin 52 (Ikkarim: "וכתב הרב ספר יוחסין שחיברו בשנת קפ"ה", used as shg), also Kaf 5, Lamed 54, Mem 105 and 139 (Manhig), Kof 62, Resh 12, Shin 109, Tav 20 (three paragraphs, on Rashi's death year). I could not read the Chida's own identification of the book's author, so that the Ayin 52 entry belongs to Zacut rests on the title "Sefer Yuchasin" (the paper dates the book to his Tunis years and the Chida cites it for dates and for the Rashi chronology); one other Samekh entry (Seder Olam Zuta, Samekh 15) mentions a "Sefer Yuchasin" in a way I did not read in full, so a second reader should confirm the identification. Disagreements: (1) death: the paper says Jerusalem or Damascus around 1515; en.wikipedia says he "probably died in 1515 in Jerusalem" and that other reports put his death in 1520 in Damascus, so the bio says Jerusalem or Damascus, around 1515 or 1520, and the era marks the death approximate (1452–כ־1515); (2) en.wikipedia dates the writing of the Sefer Yuchasin to 1504 in Tunisia, the paper to the years from 1497 in Tunis: the bio says only that he wrote it in Tunis. Years: the paper writes "1452-1515 בקירוב" and "בסביבות שנת 1515" for the death, and "בגיל 25 בלבד (בשנת 1478)", which would put the birth in 1453, and in another place says he began his main astronomical work at 21: the paper is not consistent with itself, so era is written 1452–כ־1515 (the pair the paper prints, with the death marked approximate) and no age is stated in the bio. 1478 is the date of the Chibbur, 1492 the Alhambra decree, 1496 the Portuguese decrees ("בשלהי שנת 1496"). The era_label is אחרונים (the roster's precedent for the generation of the expulsion, e.g. 679 and 573) although the year buckets say rishonim (warning only). Left out: Columbus and the eclipse of 1504 on Jamaica and his using the Almanach, which the paper tells from Wikipedia-derived sources; that is a well-known story whose historicity is disputed, and "he taught at Zaragoza and Cartagena"; the Biur Luchot / Almanach Perpetuum translation details beyond the 1496 printing; his teacher R. Yitzchak Aboab (the paper means Aboab II, d. 1493; roster 62 is Aboab I of the 14th century, a namesake, so no link) and R. Yitzchak Canpanton (59), whom the paper says he saw as a child, which is not a teacher link; R. Yaakov Berab (573), who the paper says was influenced "דרך רבי יצחק אבוהב" (not a stated relation to Zacut); the 1566 Constantinople edition; the moon crater and the museum in Tomar; his brother-in-law R. Avraham ben Eliezer HaLevi (not on the roster). Judgement calls: "historian" rests on the paper calling him a pioneer of Jewish historiography and Sefer Yuchasin his historical work; the Vasco da Gama sentence is the paper's ("זכות סיפק למשלחת את טבלאות הניווט שלו, תירגל את המלחים") and is worded "לפי הכתוב"; the astrolabe improvement is the paper's own wording and is described as "משוכלל" without the details. Place: Salamanca is not in the gazetteer; its coordinates are NOT from a fetched source (see places). No links: nothing the paper states ties him to a roster sage in a form that is a teacher/student/family/influence statement, given the Aboab namesake. SECOND READING (Q1): full hewiki/enwiki saved. Fixes: (1) bio s1: 'taught astronomy and mathematics at Salamanca' is the paper's alone; enwiki says he 'may have studied and taught astronomy' there, hewiki that he studied astronomy at the university; the sentence now says studied, and possibly taught; mathematics dropped (only the paper); (2) core s1: the quotation 'להבין דברי חז״ל וההלכות שכתבו בזה' is, in hewiki, his testimony in Sefer Yuchasin (maamar rishon, alef-bet, ot alef), not 'the introduction to his works' as the paper has it; the sentence now says Sefer Yuchasin; (3) Salamanca coordinates replaced by the Wikipedia API values (coords.json, 40.965 N 5.664 W). Checked and left: death Jerusalem/Damascus c. 1515 or 1520 (enwiki, paper; hewiki: 1513 arrival in Jerusalem, died there, '1515'); birth 12 Aug 1452 (both wikis); the Vasco da Gama sentence (enwiki states the use of his tables and astrolabe in 1497 plainly, the briefing too; hewiki: he instructed sailors in the astrolabe he improved) keeps its hedge 'לפי הכתוב'. Teacher link: hewiki and the paper name R. Yitzchak Aboab as his chief teacher; roster 62 is Aboab I of the 14th century (a namesake), the teacher is Aboab II (d. 1493), not on the roster, so no link; Canpanton (59) only seen in childhood; Vizinho not on the roster. shg: Ayin 52:1 names him only as 'the Rav (author of) Sefer Yuchasin'; identification supported by Tav 20:5, where the Chida cites Sefer Yuchasin for Rashi's death in 4865 (תתס״ה), the date Zacuto's book gives; kept.

sages.notes: Years: the owner's paper gives 1155-1215 'לערך' (circa); en.wikipedia gives only 'the second half of the 12th century' for the birth and 1204 for the settling in Toledo; no source gives an exact pair, so the row is כ־1155–1215 (the rebuild's life_years reads it as 1155, 1215) and the bio gives no birth or death year. Birthplace: the paper says Avignon, en.wikipedia 'probably at Lunel': the bio names neither (it says only that he is called HaYarchi after Lunel, which both state). Arrival in Toledo: the paper has 1194-1204, en.wikipedia 1204: the bio gives no year for it; 1204 appears only as the year he began Sefer HaManhig, where both agree (the paper's 'ד'תתקס"ד' and the Chida's 'תתקס"ד' are 4964 = 1204). Teachers: the paper has him study at Posquieres under the Ra'avad (195), en.wikipedia only 'may have studied under Abraham ben David' (in Lunel, no place for the teaching): the bio names only Dampierre and Ri HaZaken, where both agree; link 195 to 683 rests on the paper alone. Influence of the book: en.wikipedia says it 'did not exert any important influence on halakhic literature'; the paper says its influence was decisive and names Abudarham, the Tur, the Beit Yosef: neither judgement is in the bio; the links 683 to 343 (Abudarham) and 683 to 189 (Tur) rest on the paper's statements that they adopted or incorporated his rulings, and the Beit Yosef (Karo, 443) was left out as the paper there states only that Karo discussed his rulings. The relative Yitzchak ben Abba Mari (602) is named by both the paper and en.wikipedia ('a relative of Abraham's'), the relation is not further stated, so the link is family with the elder (b. 1122) as source. The colleague link 293 rests on the paper (both on the great beit din of Toledo). Maarekhet: the Chida's entry Mem 139 (Maarekhet Sefarim) is a correction of Seder HaDorot and the Pri Megadim: the author of the Manhig is Rabbenu Avraham ben Natan HaYarchi, not Raavya, and the book was written about the end of the fifth millennium (4964 = 1204); the entry names him and his book. Source limits: he.wikipedia and the Sefaria topic page could not be fetched (the fetch tool reports URL not found); the English Wikipedia text and the Maarekhet entry were obtained through a summarizing fetch tool that returns fragments of at most 125 characters, so a second reader should check the quoted fragments against the live pages. Left out: the paper's claim that his teaching passed directly into the Ramban's house of study and on to the Ramban's students (no source quoted), his translation of a responsum of Saadia Gaon (not needed), the disputed books Machazik HaBedek and Beit Zevul, and every claim about later influence on the Shulchan Aruch. Fixes: (1) bio s3: enwiki says the book consists of responsa and extracts 'in its present form'; hewiki describes the book as customs in the order of the calendar, so the sentence now says 'בצורתו הנוכחית'; (2) shg: the old quote came from paragraph 139:3 while the ref said 139:1; the shg now quotes 139:1 ('והאמת כי מחבר המנהיג רבינו אברהם ן׳ ירחי'), which names him and his book; (3) hewiki added as a source: born in Lunel (enwiki 'probably'; the paper says Avignon: the bio names none), teacher Ri HaZaken at Dampierre, colleague link with the Ramah on the Toledo beit din (hewiki and paper), wandering then Toledo; hewiki says he reached Toledo about age 40 and returned there in 1211 after a stay in Provence, the paper 1194-1204: the bio gives no year for it. Years כ־1155–1215 agree in hewiki, enwiki ('second half of 12th c.') and the paper. Links kept: Ravad 195 is the paper's statement alone (enwiki 'may have studied under Abraham ben David'; hewiki does not list him among his teachers: Ri HaZaken, his son Elchanan, Yedidiah of Melun, Chaim b. Chananel HaCohen of Paris, none but Ri on the roster); 602 relative (enwiki, paper); 266, 343, 189 influence (paper); 293 colleague (hewiki, paper). Alfasi (582) and Ibn Ghiyyat (352): the book contains extracts from their works (enwiki), not stated as influence, so no link.

sages.notes: Years: en.wikipedia (1549-1639) and the Sefaria topic ('born in 1549 in Modena', no death year) give 1549 for the birth; the owner's paper gives the death, 26 Tammuz 5399 = 28 July 1639, and says that the sources differ on the birth year, some placing it in 1549 (5309) and others about 1585 (5345 by the paper's 'ה'שמ"ח'). Because the paper itself reports the dispute the row is written כ־1549–1639 (the rebuild's life_years reads 1549, 1639) and the bio gives no birth or death year; the only years in the bio are 1624 and 1626 (the printing of Ashmoret HaBoker and Maavar Yabbok, which the paper and en.wikipedia both give). Relatives: en.wikipedia calls him a nephew of Rabbi Yehuda Aryeh of Modena (Leon Modena, 78), the paper calls him his cousin on his mother's side; the sources disagree on the relation and Leon (b. 1571) is the younger man, so no family link was recorded and the relation is not in the bio. His brother-in-law Yosef Yedidya Carmi and his teacher Hillel of Modena are not on the roster. Teachers: en.wikipedia and the paper agree on Hillel of Modena, the Rama of Fano (439) and Israel Sarug (467; Sarug a student of the Ari); the paper calls the Rama his 'מורו המובהק בחכמת הקבלה' and adds that popular sources sometimes confuse him with the Remez, which is not used. Left out: the arrest of 1636 for owning books (en.wikipedia; true as sourced but not a central fact), the pupils Hillel his son and Shabtai Baer (the paper alone, neither is on the roster), the polemic with Carmi over the prayer text (the paper alone), the paper's mention of a heavenly maggid reported by the Chida, and the paper's literary echoes (Peretz, Sholem Aleichem, Halkin, Alterman, the Tel Aviv street). The paper's account of the book's five sections and of the name's gematria (112 chapters, 'יחוד, ברכה, קדושה') is not in the core idea. Influence link 684 to 126: the paper quotes the Ben Ish Chai adopting many practices from Maavar Yabbok. Maarekhet: the Chida lists the book 'Maavar Yabbok' in Maarekhet Sefarim (Mem 164) as by 'כמהר"ר אהרן ברכיה ממודינא' and refers to his article in Maarekhet Gedolim, volume one (not on Sefaria); the same cross-reference stands in Alef 116 (Imrei Shefer, one of his manuscripts): the entry names him and his book, with no more text. Source limits: he.wikipedia could not be fetched (the fetch tool reports URL not found); the English Wikipedia, Sefaria and Maarekhet texts were obtained through a summarizing fetch tool that returns fragments of at most 125 characters, so a second reader should check the quoted fragments against the live pages. SECOND READING (Q1): full hewiki/enwiki/Sefaria texts saved and used (the Sefaria URL corrected to sefaria.org/topics/...). Fixes: bio s3 said the group was 'Lurianic' and 'founded by him'; enwiki says so, but Sefaria says he wrote it 'at the request of a local group' and hewiki says only that he wrote it for the group 'Meirei HaShachar' in Modena, so the sentence now says 'for a group of early risers in Modena' (hewiki, Sefaria, paper agree). Checked and left: bio s1 (Mantua burial society request, 'primary source text' enwiki; paper 'ספר היסוד'); bio s2: hewiki says he studied with Hillel and the Rama of Fano and 'was close to' Israel Sarug, enwiki and the paper say he studied with Sarug (kept, from enwiki and the paper); core s1 'in the introduction' is the paper's 'בהקדמתו' (quote added); core s2 is attributed to the site's research. Dates: hewiki 1549 – 26 Tammuz 5399 (28 July 1639), enwiki 1549-1639, Sefaria 1549; the paper reports the dispute (1549 or c. 1585), so כ־1549–1639 stands; with 1585 the teacher link to the Rama of Fano (1548-1620) would be natural, with 1549 it is a one-year gap (validator warning, both enwiki and hewiki and the paper name him as teacher). sages.notes: Years: the owner's paper puts him 'around 680-752' (the sources it cites are not dated), en.wikipedia says he left Babylonia about 752 or 753 and lived in Israel until his death, 'the exact date of his death is unknown' (Steinschneider's 761 is called erroneous), and Sefaria gives only 'eighth-century': (correction by the second reader: hewiki 'ד׳ת״מ (680) לערך – סביבות ד׳תק״כ (760)', Sefaria birth 680 (approximate) and death 752, and the paper 'סביב השנים 680–752' DO give a birth year, c. 680, and for death 752 (Sefaria, paper; but enwiki and the paper say he left Babylonia only in 750-753 and lived on in Israel, and hewiki says c. 760); the century stays because the death is not secure and he lived in the eighth century in every source), so the row is the century, המאה ה־8, and the bio has no year. Dating of the move: the paper says about 750-753, en.wikipedia 752 or 753; the bio says only that he went up to the Land of Israel. Natronai: the paper and en.wikipedia agree that the exilarch Solomon bar Chasdai, out of a personal grudge, passed Achai over for the Pumbedita geonate and appointed Natronai Kahana ben Amuna, Achai's student ('underling' in en.wikipedia, 'תלמידו ומשמשו' in the paper); Natronai is not on the roster, so there is no teacher link. The paper's own slip, 'a move that caused Achai's retirement to Babylonia' (it means the Land of Israel, as the same paper says elsewhere), is not used. Identity: the paper separates him from the Savoraic Rav Achai (c. 500-515), who is not him. The 'about 190 units' and the four-part structure of a she'ilta are the paper's; en.wikipedia only says 'a collection of homilies on Jewish law and ethics'. Influence links 685 to 21, 25, 594, 582, 41 rest on one sentence of the paper naming the later authorities who 'quote the Sheiltot often' (Rav Sherira, Rav Hai, Rashi, Rashbam, the Tosafists, the Rif, the Rambam, the Ramban): it is the book that they quote, so the link is influence only; 276 (Rashbam) and 44 (Ramban) are on the roster but were left out to keep the links to five. The link 685 to 680 rests on the paper's statement that Halachot Pesukot, 'attributed to Rav Yehudai Gaon', and the Halachot Gedolot drew on the Sheiltot: the attribution is the paper's word and the bio keeps it as 'geonic books of rulings such as Halachot Pesukot'. Maarekhet: the Sheiltot have no entry of their own in the Chida's Maarekhet Sefarim as Sefaria holds it (the letters Shin, Resh, Alef and He were searched for שאילתות, שאלתות and אחאי; the Chida spells it שאלתות or discusses it under Rav Achai in Maarekhet Gedolim, volume one, which Sefaria does not have). sages.notes: See the report. Sources: the owner's paper 686 (primary); en.wikipedia (David_ben_Abraham_Oppenheim); the Sefaria topic david-oppenheim (birthYear 1664, deathYear 1736); the Chida, Maarekhet Sefarim Nun 47 (the book Nishal David, responsa of "מהר"ד אופנהיים"). He.wikipedia could not be fetched from this environment (every he.wikipedia URL returned URL_NOT_FOUND), so no source of kind he.wikipedia is recorded. Years 1664-1736: paper (Sivan 5424 = June 1664; 7 Tishrei 5497 = 12 September 1736, age 72), en.wikipedia (1664 - 12 September 1736) and Sefaria all agree; written as exact years. Years of his appointments are left out of the bio because the sources disagree (paper: Nikolsburg 1689, Prague 1702 / chief rabbi 1712; en.wikipedia: Nikolsburg 1691, Prague 1703, half of Moravia 1713, all by 1718). Teachers: en.wikipedia lists Yair Bacharach first among his teachers, the paper calls the relation a deep friendship with a rich correspondence ("קשר ידידות עמוקה") and gives as his chief teacher Gershon Ashkenazi of Metz (not on the roster); the link 657->686 is recorded as teacher on the strength of en.wikipedia only. Reischer: the paper (and the roster entry 660) call him his brother-in-law; Reischer (c.1661) is the elder, so he is the source of the family link. The Chida says "ס' נשאל דוד ושאר חידושיו לא נדפסו" while the paper says part of Nishal David was printed at Dessau in 1708: the core idea says only that he did not print most of his twenty books in his lifetime (the paper) and names Nishal David as one of them (the Chida). Left out: the title "נשיא ארץ ישראל", the reason the paper gives for storing the library in Hanover (escaping the Prague censorship: a cause stated from secondary sources), the size of the library (the paper gives 4,220-4,500 printed books and 750-780 manuscripts, with its own spread), the 1829 price (the paper: 2,080 pounds, about 9,000 thalers; en.wikipedia: 9,000 thalers), the halakhic rulings, Teplitsky's book. Not linked although the sources state a relation: Eybeschutz (653; the paper says only "מקורב משפחתית"), Meir Eisenstadt (688; one paper says he studied with Oppenheim: recorded under 688 as a judgement call, see its notes), Chaim Jonah Teomim (son-in-law, not on the roster). SECOND READING (Q2): full he.wikipedia (rev 43953088) and en.wikipedia (David_Oppenheim_(rabbi), rev 1369224435; the writer's URL was a redirect) now saved as sources. He.wikipedia agrees on 1664 Worms - 7 Tishrei 5497 Prague, Nikolsburg then Prague, the Old Jewish Cemetery, about twenty books, Nishal David printed in his lifetime (the rest in manuscript), the Bodleian library; it says he studied with Gershon Ashkenazi and others and was a FRIEND of Yair Bacharach (corresponded with him), while en.wikipedia lists Bacharach among his teachers: the teacher link 657->686 rests on en.wikipedia alone and is kept with that caveat (both can be true). He.wikipedia does not mention Hanover or the lessons; those two statements rest on the owner's paper only (the paper gives a censorship motive for Hanover, left out). No sentence changed.

Yedidya Shlomo of Norzi, one of the rabbis of Mantua; mentions Lonzano and his Or Torah). He.wikipedia could not be fetched from this environment (URL_NOT_FOUND), so no he.wikipedia source is recorded. Years: the paper says "סביבות 1560 – לאחר 1626", en.wikipedia and Sefaria give 1560-1626, but the only dated event in 1626 that any source states is the completion of the book (en.wikipedia: "The work was completed in 1626"; paper: Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5386 = 1626) and the paper says he lived after it. Written as כ־1560–1626 (the rebuild reads 1560 and 1626 as the pair), the bio gives no death year and says only that the book was completed in 1626. Ordination 1585: en.wikipedia and the paper agree. "Born in Mantua": en.wikipedia only (the paper says only that the Norzi family branched out to Mantua and Ferrara); the Chida calls him one of the rabbis of Mantua. The paper says he was chosen at the beginning of the 17th century as a member of the court and teacher in Mantua; en.wikipedia says co-rabbi: the bio says "one of the rabbis of the city" (the Chida). The title Minchat Shai: en.wikipedia and the paper say it was given at the first printing (Mantua 1742-44, Raphael Chaim Basila); Sefaria says the book was published posthumously under that name. The paper also says "twenty-one books of the Bible" in one place and "twenty-four" in another; neither number is used. Links: Lonzano (654) and Meir Abulafia (293, the Rama) are stated by en.wikipedia (and by the paper) as influences on Norzi, direction source influenced target. His teacher Moses Cases is not on the roster. Left out: the 330-source hierarchy and the manuscript list (paper only, figures not cross-checked), the book "גדר הגדול" (paper only), the 21st-century edition by Bezer and Ofer, the Kabbalistic reading of the differences between the Masorah and the Sages. SECOND READING (Q2): full he.wikipedia (rev 42920448), en.wikipedia (rev 1327907322) and the Sefaria topic saved. He.wikipedia: born 1560 in Mantua, died 'after 5386 (1626)' (so the end of the era is the completion year, as the notes say), ordained 1585, chosen rabbi of Mantua toward 1600; it wrongly limits Goder Peretz to the Pentateuch and dates the first printing 1741 (enwiki and the paper: 1742-44, kept). Born in Mantua is now supported by both wikis and Sefaria. Fixed: 'traditional and critical commentary' (Hebrew מסורתי means 'traditional', the sources say Masoretic = about the Masorah) now says a critical commentary concerned with the Masorah and the text; the three languages agree. Sefaria says 'published posthumously under the name Minchat Shai', consistent with the bio.

sages.notes: Sources: the owner's paper 688 (primary), the Sefaria topic meir-eisenstadt (birthYear 1670, deathYear 1744; the English description is the source of the stations and of Eybeschutz as best-known student), en.wikipedia (Meir_Eisenstadt; only fragments of it were seen: 'c. 1670 in Poznań', '1744 in Eisenstadt', the names of Panim Meirot and Kotnot Or), and the Chida, Maarekhet Sefarim Peh 104 (Panim Meirot: 'the Gaon R. Meir av beit din of Eisenstadt, grandson of the sister of the Gaon the Shach'; three parts of responsa and novellae on Zevachim, Kiddushin and Gittin, a fourth on Bava Kamma; his rabbi was R. Moshe av beit din of Sochatchov; his daughter's son R. Elazar [Kalir] wrote Or Chadash; the Or HaGanuz survived from his lost works). He.wikipedia could not be fetched from this environment (URL_NOT_FOUND), so no he.wikipedia source is recorded (the paper cites it). Years: all sources give 1744 for his death (paper: 27 Sivan 5504). For birth the paper says 'around 5430 (1670)', en.wikipedia 'c. 1670', Sefaria 1670; written as כ־1670–1744. Stations: the paper puts Szydłowiec, Worms (1700, scattered 1701), Prostějov (1702-1717), a second term in Szydłowiec, Eisenstadt (1717); Sefaria has the same order without dates but says he served as dayan in Posen first. The bio lists the stations without dates. Teachers: the paper names Abraham Abele Gombiner (84) as his chief teacher in youth and says he was deeply influenced by visits to and study with David Oppenheim (686); the Chida names as his rabbi R. Moshe av beit din of Sochatchov (whom the paper makes his father-in-law, R. Moshe Sachtschwer of Posen), and Sefaria and en.wikipedia name no teacher. Gombiner died in 1682 when he was about twelve, Oppenheim was six years older than he, and the three accounts do not agree, so NO teacher link was recorded for either (judgement: dropped_links candidates 84->688 and 686->688, each from the paper alone) and the bio names no teacher. Recorded links: 688 -> 653 teacher (Sefaria: his best known student is probably Eybeschutz; the paper says the same), and 83 -> 688 family (the Chida: 'נכד אחות הגאון הרב שפתי כהן', the Shach being the elder relative). Not linked: Chacham Tzvi (693), whom the Chida and the paper call his 'מחותן' (co-parent-in-law, left out by the convention of the paper-links file); his grandson R. Elazar Kalir and his descendants (Pitchei Teshuva, Netziv: not on the roster). Left out of the bio: the false denunciation of 1723 and the flight to Poland (the paper only, sourced from forum and encyclopaedia pages), the card-playing ordinance, the Prossnitz affair (Leibele Prossnitz), the descendants, the distinction from R. Meir Eisenstadter (Maharam Ash of Ungvar, 1780-1852; the paper takes pains to separate the two, the roster has only this one), the claim that the 'ash' in Meore Esh stands for Eisenstadt (the Sefaria text says so too, but the point is the book's name, not his). SECOND READING (Q2): full he.wikipedia (rev 43931229), en.wikipedia (rev 1253376412) and the Sefaria topic saved. All three bio sentences and both core sentences checked: stations in the order of Sefaria/en.wikipedia (Szydlowiec, Worms, Prostejov, Eisenstadt), Eybeschutz among his students (Sefaria: best known; he.wikipedia: he raised him and was his father and teacher), 1744 death in Eisenstadt (he.wikipedia: 27 Sivan 5504, buried in the old cemetery), 1670 birth in Poznan (he.wikipedia: 5430 = 1670; en.wikipedia c. 1670), responsa Panim Meirot and Kotnot Or, consulted by rabbis from Turkey, Germany and Italy (Sefaria and en.wikipedia); 'caution and adherence to the wording of the sources' rests on the owner's paper alone (kept, it is the paper's own characterisation). No sentence changed. Links: he.wikipedia now states that in his youth he studied with Gombiner (84) and with 'David Oppenheimer' (taken to be Oppenheim 686, as the paper says), which the writer had found only in the paper; teacher link 84 -> 688 added (he.wikipedia and the paper). 686 -> 688 NOT added: the paper's 'study with Oppenheim' is the only clear source, he.wikipedia's 'David Oppenheimer' is ambiguous, and Oppenheim was born only six years before him. Caveat: Gombiner died in 1682 when Meir was about twelve, so 'in his youth' means childhood study; the dates do not contradict it. The Shach (83) family link is also in he.wikipedia ('נכד אחותו של הרב שבתי הכהן, הש"ך'). Chacham Tzvi (693) stays unlinked (co-parents-in-law).

sages.notes: Sources: the owner's paper 689 (primary); full he.wikipedia (rev 43796726), en.wikipedia (Meir_Schiff, rev 1277582351, from the 1906 Jewish Encyclopedia) and the Sefaria topic. Maarekhet/Gedolim: Maarekhet Sefarim has no entry for his book (Chiddushei Halachot, printed 1737, after the Chida's source period; the search for שיף, מהר"ם שיף and the Fulda yeshiva found nothing else), but Letter Chet 57:1 is a cross-reference entry 'חידושים - על ש"ס וד' טורים. (עיין מ' מאיר שיף בח"א)': it names him ('מאיר שיף', with a pointer to his entry in Maarekhet Gedolim, part one, not in the saved file) and matches the notes on the Shas and the four Turim that Sefaria lists; used as the shg, with that limit. Years: the paper and he.wikipedia give death 21 Adar 5401 (2 March 1641) and birth 1605 (he.wikipedia: 'traditions differ, apparently 1608'); en.wikipedia and Sefaria give 1608-1644. The sources disagree by three years, so the row says only 'המאה ה־17' (century window) and the bio says 'the first half of the 17th century' (true on every reckoning) and gives no year. 'About seventeen' when called to Fulda: the paper, en.wikipedia and Sefaria say seventeen; he.wikipedia says 1622, which with its birth year 1608 would be fourteen: the age is kept as the three sources give it. SECOND READING (Q2) FIXES: (1) bio sentence 1 'one of the prominent sages of Ashkenaz and luminary of the Talmud' was the paper's evaluation alone; replaced by what he.wikipedia says (yeshiva head and Talmud commentator in Germany, known for his great sharpness). (2) bio sentence 3 'the Prague leaders offered him the rabbinate, he fell ill and died before he could settle' (paper) became 'shortly before his death he was called to be rabbi of Prague, but died suddenly at a young age' (he.wikipedia 'נתמנה', en.wikipedia 'called', paper 'offered'; 'fell ill' is the paper's only). (3) core sentence 2 'subordinated logical sharpness to a precise understanding of the language of the Talmud, Rashi and the Tosafot' (paper) contradicts he.wikipedia, which makes him a symbol of sharpness and not one who cross-checks sources; replaced by he.wikipedia's 'a deep local understanding of the passage and of the Tosafot'; and 'printed at the end of the tractates of the Shas in the Vilna edition' was too wide: he.wikipedia says at the end of some of the tractates (the paper says 'of every tractate'). Kept: eleven tractates (he.wikipedia '11'; en.wikipedia lists about ten), condensed lessons of the Fulda yeshiva. First edition: the paper says Zolkva 5484 (1723/24, also the he.wikipedia title page), en.wikipedia 1737 at Homburg: no printing date given. Teacher link 599 (the Shelah) -> 689 rests on the owner's paper alone (neither wikipedia names a teacher); kept. Left out: marriage and children, the 1711 fire (he.wikipedia gives 24 Tevet 5471), the Prague rabbinate's date, the influence on later authorities, teachers not on the roster. Location 'גרמניה' stays because lib/regions.ts has no keyword for Frankfurt or Fulda (the lead may add them).

sages.notes: Maarekhet/Gedolim: shg is null because the Shem HaGedolim text on Sefaria and Wikisource could not be reached from this worker (sefaria.org and he.wikisource.org are refused by the shell proxy; WebFetch returned errors or paraphrased summaries only), so no entry of Maarekhet Sefarim / Maarekhet Gedolim could be quoted; the Chida names him "רב נסים גאון" and his book "מפתח" (to be checked by the lead with a tool that returns the page text). Sources: only the owner's paper (public/research/690.json); his Hebrew and English Wikipedia articles and his Sefaria page could not be saved verbatim (Hebrew Wikipedia is blocked for this session, WebFetch paraphrases), so nothing from them is quoted. Years: the paper gives "בסביבות שנת 990" for his birth and "בסביבות שנת 1062" for his death; both are approximate, so the row reads כ־990–1062. Left out: the family-name claim (Persian roots of "אבן שהין"), his mother being of the family of Dunash ben Labrat (198) and his father-in-law Dunash (the paper says both; a mother from Dunash's family and a father-in-law Dunash cannot both be taken at face value, so no link to 198 is proposed), the marriage of his daughter to Yosef son of Shmuel HaNagid in 1049 and her flight after 1066 (a co-parent-in-law tie, not a teacher/family link between the two sages), the Rif as his student (the paper itself says the Rif was not a direct student, only influenced through the books: proposed as influence 690 -> 582), the Lulav-laws polemic against the Karaites, his Torah commentary and Sefer HaMitzvot (the paper says they are lost). Links: 35 is "חברו וידידו, רבנו חננאל בן חושיאל" (colleague; the roster gives Chananel only "מאה 11"); 25 (Rav Hai Gaon) is the authority whose position Nissim relied on (influence 25 -> 690); 582, 41, 683 and 602 are the paper's statements of who relied on or quoted him (influence 690 -> each). 683 (the Hamanhig) is a new id from another worker (N2): drop that link if 683 is not integrated. Teacher links: Chushiel ben Elchanan and Nissim's father are not on the roster. The gaon title: the paper says he was not a gaon of a Babylonian yeshiva but was given the title by his contemporaries. SECOND READING (Q2): NOTE the saved wiki/690.hewiki.txt and 690.enwiki.txt are the WRONG person (Nessim Gaon, the 20th-century financier; the page for Rav Nissim Gaon is he.wikipedia 'רב ניסים גאון' / en 'Nissim ben Jacob'), so they were not used; he.wikipedia/en.wikipedia could not be saved verbatim for this sage (a live WebFetch of en.wikipedia Nissim_ben_Jacob returned only a summary: 990-1062, studied under his father Jacob ben Nissim and Chushiel, headed the yeshiva with Chananel ben Chushiel, corresponded with Hai ben Sherira and Samuel ibn Naghrillah, son Joseph married his daughter in 1049, works Mafteach, Hibbur Yafeh, Megillat Setarim, Rif his most famous student), consistent with the record but not quotable. Added as sources: the Sefaria topic nissim-gaon (verbatim: leader of Kairouan, learned from his father and Chushiel, corresponded with Hai and Shmuel HaNagid) and two Shem HaGedolim entries: Mem 192:1 (ספר מפתח, by 'רבינו נסים בן רבינו יעקב', on all tractates, explaining the unspoken parts of the Talmud, the basis mainly Bavli and Yerushalmi) is now the shg; Mem 49:1 (מגלת סתרים, by Rabbeinu Nissim Gaon, mentioned by the Tosafot and the Rishonim; the Chida adds that the Megillat Setarim seems to be the work of Nissim ben Yaakov ben Shahin, friend of Rabbeinu Chananel, who learned from Hai's writings and was therefore called Gaon, and that he did not find him listed among the Geonim). FIXES: bio sentence 2 said he 'served as a link between Rav Hai Gaon and Shmuel HaNagid' (paper only; Sefaria says he corresponded with both): now 'corresponded with Rav Hai Gaon and with Shmuel HaNagid in Granada' in all three languages. Core sentence 2 ('widely quoted among the Rishonim') rests on the paper plus the Chida's 'mentioned by the Tosafot and the Rishonim in several places': kept. The Gaon-title sentence is the paper's (the Chida gives a different reason: that he learned from Hai's writings); the bio states only that his contemporaries called him Gaon although he held no Babylonian gaonate, as the paper does. The Rif link 690 -> 582 stays influence (Sefaria: his most famous student; the paper: not a direct student), the three others as the paper states. Dates כ־990–1062 stay (Sefaria 990/1062, the paper 'around'). || SECOND READING (Q2), REDONE against the right articles (he.wikipedia 'רב ניסים גאון' rev 41822443, en.wikipedia 'Nissim ben Jacob' rev 1378748810, now sources; the earlier remark that they could not be saved is superseded). Verdicts: bio s1 'his contemporaries gave him the title Gaon' IMPRECISE: he.wikipedia says only that he was called so, as a title of honour, since he headed a yeshiva rated equal to the Babylonian ones (the Chida gives yet another reason); now 'called Gaon as a title of honour although he held no Babylonian gaonate', he/en/ru. Bio s2 correct (father, then Chushiel, with Chananel; correspondence with Hai and Shmuel HaNagid: both wikis). Bio s3 IMPRECISE: 'because of the political and security unrest he had to leave' is the paper's cause; he.wikipedia says Kairouan was plundered and destroyed in his time and he moved to Mahdia, where he died in 1062: now that, he/en/ru. Core s1 'above all the Jerusalem Talmud' IMPRECISE: en.wikipedia lists the Tosefta, Mekhilta, Sifre, Sifra and the Yerushalmi; now 'among them the Jerusalem Talmud'. Core s2 'widely quoted among the Rishonim' for the Megillat Setarim IMPRECISE (a scope the sources do not give): now the Chida's 'mentioned by the Tosafot and the Rishonim in several places'. Hibbur Yafeh as a book of consolation in Judeo-Arabic correct (he.wikipedia: sent to console his father-in-law Dunash, written in Arabic; en.wikipedia: Judeo-Arabic). Years: he.wikipedia 'around 990 - 1062', en.wikipedia 990-1062, Sefaria 990-1062: כ־990–1062 kept. Links: 35 colleague kept (en.wikipedia: closely associated with Chananel; he.wikipedia: studied alongside him; paper: friend); 25 influence kept; 41, 683, 602 rest on the paper alone, kept; 582 stays influence although he.wikipedia, en.wikipedia ('probably') and Sefaria name the Rif as his student, because the paper (Rapoport) says he was not a direct student; either reading fits an influence link; ADDED 690 -> 597 colleague (Shmuel HaNagid: both wikis state an active correspondence); Dunash (198) still not linked (the roster's Dunash ben Labrat, 920-990, is not shown to be his father-in-law).

sages.notes: SECOND READING (Q2). Sources: the owner's paper 691 (primary); full he.wikipedia (rev 43363716), en.wikipedia (rev 1343563076), the Sefaria topic nathan-nota-spira and the Chida's Maarekhet Sefarim Mem 45:1 ('מגלה עמוקות - ספר נפלא מהגאון המקובל מהר"ן שפירא רנ"ב אופנים על פ' ואתחנן ... וחיבר אלף אופנים על אל"ף דויקרא זעירא'; the Chida also says a maggid was told of the author; not used). Years: the paper 5345 / 1584-85 and 13 Av 5393 = 20 July 1633 at about 48; he.wikipedia '~1584' and 20 July 1633; en.wikipedia and Sefaria 1585-1633; written כ־1585–1633. Born in Hrodna: the paper only (he.wikipedia says his grandfather was rabbi of Horodna and that he moved from Horodna to Kazimierz about 1608; it does not say where he was born); kept. He.wikipedia: appointed head of the yeshiva and preacher of Kraków in 1617 (age 31) in place of R. Moshe Mordechai Margaliot, buried in the old cemetery of Kraków, his father-in-law supplied all his needs so he held his public offices without pay, 252 ways of Moses' prayer, 'Chiddushei Anshei Shem' on the Rif, 'the greatest of his students was R. Shabtai Kohen (the Shach)', and R. Yonatan Eybeschutz among his descendants. FIXES: (1) bio sentence 1 said he was 'known for his writings on Kabbalah and halakha'; every source makes him known chiefly as a kabbalist and by his Megaleh Amukot (the paper: his name spread mainly through his Kabbalistic work, although he was also a giant in halakha): now 'known above all as a kabbalist and as the author of Megaleh Amukot' in the three languages. (2) bio sentence 2: 'undertook to support him, and so he could teach students and study without material worry' stated a purpose and an undertaking; he.wikipedia and Sefaria say the father-in-law supplied his needs and he therefore filled his public posts without pay (en.wikipedia: refused a salary): now that, in the three languages. (3) core sentence 2 said 'glosses and novellae on the Rif and the Ran'; he.wikipedia, Sefaria and the Chida's citations name only the Rif (the paper says Rif and Ran): now the Rif only. Kept: 'in the prime of life, at about forty-eight' (paper; the births 1584/85 and 1633 give 48-49). Links: family 691 -> 653 (Eybeschutz is listed among his descendants in he.wikipedia; the paper's list says the same; the exact line is not stated); teacher 691 -> 83 ADDED (he.wikipedia: 'גדול תלמידיו היה רבי שבתי כהן (הש"ך)'; the paper says the same; the writer wrongly thought the Shach was not on the roster, he is 83; the Shach was born in 1622, so he was a child when Natan Nata died: the dates do not contradict it, but the claim is the sources', not ours); colleague 691 <-> 76 (the Bach) rests on the paper alone and is kept. Not linked: Meir of Lublin (enwiki: he was his student; the paper lists the Maharam of Lublin among his teachers; not on the roster), Margaliot (not on the roster).

sages.notes: Second reading (Q3). Full texts: he.wikipedia (810 approx.-875 approx.; head of Sura 853-872), en.wikipedia (d. 875; gaon from c. 857, 18 years), Sefaria topic (810-875), the owner's paper (gaon c. 857/858-875). Sources disagree on the gaonate's start and give a birth year (c. 810) only in he.wikipedia and Sefaria, so the row keeps the century (birth_year/death_year 800/900 are the century window) and the bio states no year. Responsa: en.wikipedia says he is the author of about 120 (most printed in Shaarei Tzedek, Salonica 1792); the paper says 120 to 200 survive; the bio says only what en.wikipedia says (authored, not survived). The Seder: the paper calls it the earliest complete prayer book to reach us; en.wikipedia adds that the surviving text is heavily edited and that Spain never adopted it as a whole, so the core idea says one of the foundations (Sephardic: 'basis for the Sephardic prayer tradition'; Ashkenazic: 'major source used in the standardization of nusach Ashkenaz'), not the foundation. The community: the paper and he.wikipedia say Barcelona (the paper: probably), the bio says only Spain. Shem HaGedolim: Maarekhet Sefarim Samekh 17 names Rav Amram bar Sheshna and his Seder; Yod 47 (Yesod HaAmrami: the author of HaManhig's name for the Seder) also names it. Links (influence, source influenced target): the Rif (582), the Rambam, Abudraham (343) and the Yarchi (683) relied on the Seder according to the paper (the Raavad it names is left out: two Raavads on the roster); en.wikipedia: the Seder served as the model for Saadia's (344) and Maimonides' (41) prayer texts. Left out: the paper's 872 for the Seder, the cities Barcelona/Elisana, 'between 120 and 200' responsa, Rabbeinu Tam's quotation, the hekhalot layers, the editions.

sages.notes: Second reading (Q3), against the full he.wikipedia, en.wikipedia, Sefaria topic and the owner's paper. YEARS: he.wikipedia and the paper put his birth on 1 Elul 5418 (30 August 1658, Trebitsch); en.wikipedia and Sefaria say 1656; all give death on 1 Iyar 5478 (2/3 May 1718), so the row reads כ־1656–1718 and the bio gives only 1718 (birth_year 1656 is the row's convention for the earlier of the two). Birthplace: Trebitsch (he.wikipedia, paper) or most likely Gross Meseritsch (en.wikipedia), both Moravia, so the bio says only Moravia. Hakham title: en.wikipedia and Sefaria place it in Istanbul/Constantinople (the paper: ordained by the Great Court of Constantinople before 18). Amsterdam: letter of appointment 10 January 1710 (en.wikipedia), 1710 (paper); the bio leaves it out. THE HAYYUN SENTENCE (corrected): the first version said Ashkenazi himself 'identified disguised Sabbatean quotations' in Hayyun's writings, which is the paper's account only; en.wikipedia says Moses Hagiz discovered the Sabbatean principles and alerted Ashkenazi (who had first taken Hayyun for an old enemy and retracted), so the bio now says only that the writings were suspected of Sabbatean principles; the ban was on 23 July 1713 (en.wikipedia). He left Amsterdam at the beginning of 1714 (en.wikipedia; the paper: 5474/1714). The hen: the paper says an animal 'with a blood system' cannot live a moment without a heart (the first version said any animal); the paper dates the dispute to AHU 1709; he.wikipedia says the dispute made him resign the AHU post. Shem HaGedolim: Maarekhet Sefarim has no entry for the book Chacham Tzvi; the only mention is the name 'הג"מ צבי אשכני' in the list of authors of responsa (Shin 6:1: 'שאלות ותשובות'); the identification with the Chacham Tzvi rests on that list being of responsa authors and on the surname-name match, and Peh 105 (Pesach Gadol) refers to an entry 'Tzvi Ashkenazi' in the Chida's volume 1, so this is a name-only mention, kept as weak. Links: family 693 -> 89 (Jacob Emden, his son: en.wikipedia) and teacher 693 -> 89 (he.wikipedia: 'אביו ורבו'); colleague 86 (Moshe Hagiz) - 693: en.wikipedia 'Hagiz fought valiantly beside Ashkenazi', he.wikipedia 'יחד עם רבי משה חגיז'. Not linked: David Nieto (487, 1705 ruling: en.wikipedia says he was invited to pronounce a decision, not what it was; the paper alone says he cleared him), the Taz (79), Shmuel Abuhav (663, hospitality only); Kovo, Ephraim ha-Kohen, Rothenburg, Ayllon are not on the roster. Left out: descendants, 2,500 guilders, Ofen siege, the Berlin marriage, the golem responsum, students (David Frankel: paper only).

sages.notes: Second reading (Q3), against the full he.wikipedia, the Sefaria topic and the owner's paper (no English Wikipedia article exists; the Jewish Virtual Library page could not be fetched in full from this environment, so its earlier short extracts are no longer used as sources). YEARS: he.wikipedia and Sefaria give 1525-1595; the paper 1525 - about 1595 (בקירוב); the row keeps כ־1525–1595 (the paper hedges the death), the bio states no birth/death year and gives only the century and the printing year 1597. 1597: the paper says the Genesis volume of the Yefe Toar was first printed in Venice in 1597, two years after the author's death, and he.wikipedia's list of editions has 'Venice 5357 (1597)'. He.wikipedia: he was the pupil of 'Rabbi Yitzchak ben Lev' and Rabbi Shlomo Alkabetz; the paper names the same two (the first as 'Rabbi Yitzchak ben Lev (the Maharival)', a name that does not match the roster's 640, Yosef ibn Lev), so the link to 640 is DROPPED (the sources say Yitzchak, the roster's man is Yosef; the earlier JVL 'Joseph Leib' could not be re-checked) and the link from Alkabetz (327, 1505-1584) is ADDED (he.wikipedia: 'היה תלמידם של ... רבי שלמה אלקבץ'). Corrections: the core idea's methodological claim (Talmudic methods brought to midrash, textual variants, resolving difficulties) and the 'more than two hundred years' of printing are stated only by the owner's paper, so they now say 'according to the research paper'; the Chida says the Yefe Toar was not printed on Bamidbar and Devarim, so the bio does not say all of the Torah was printed. Shem HaGedolim Yod 54: 'מהר"ש יפה' as author of Yefe Mareh, printed in Venice in his lifetime (Yod 56-58 name the Yefe Anaf, Kol and Toar as 'מהרב ז"ל', the same man). Left out: the family tie to the Levush (73) and to the Bach's father (he.wikipedia: 'some think'; the paper: 'research points to'), the 1549/50 move, the lost Even HaEzer commentary, the Beit Din Yafe, Plungian's abridgement.

YEARS: he.wikipedia 1150-1230, en.wikipedia c. 1150 - c. 1230 (Lunel - Marseille), the paper 1150-1230 'בקירוב'; the row keeps כ־1150–1230 and the bio says 'around 1230'. he.wikipedia also reports an opinion that he died at 80 and a burial tradition in Tiberias (left out). 1204: en.wikipedia 'Guide ... in 1204', the paper 'completed in 1204, the year of the Rambam's death'; he.wikipedia says he translated it in Maimonides' lifetime (consistent). 1213 for the lexicon (he.wikipedia, en.wikipedia, paper) is not used. SHEM HAGEDOLIM (was null, now found): Maarekhet Sefarim Yod 60:1 'יקוו המים - מאמר. (עיין הרב שמואל ן' תבון בח"א)' names him and his book Ma'amar Yikavu HaMayim; Mem 134 and Peh 39 also mention him. Corrections: (1) the first bio sentence ended 'who was active in Lunel...' with the relative clause attached to the father in Hebrew and English, so the places are now a sentence of their own (paper: Lunel, Montpellier, Béziers, Marseille; en.wikipedia: Lunel, Béziers 1199, Arles 1204, Marseille); (2) the core idea's two evaluative claims (the tools to philosophize in Hebrew; first to see the Guide as built on deliberate contradictions) are stated only by the paper, so they now say 'according to the research paper' (the Ravitzky attribution is the paper's, and he.wikipedia lists Ravitzky's article 'R. Shmuel ibn Tibbon and the secret of the Guide'; he.wikipedia says only that Ibn Tibbon attributed to the Rambam agreement with the Aristotelian position). Not linked: Yehuda ibn Tibbon (father), Moshe (son), Jacob Anatoli (son-in-law, a student per the paper): none on the roster; Abraham ben HaRambam (600) only reports the Rambam's opinion of him. sages.notes: Second reading (Q3), against the full he.wikipedia, en.wikipedia, the Sefaria topic and the owner's paper. YEARS DISAGREE ON DEATH: he.wikipedia 'בערך 1150 − 1214'; en.wikipedia 'c. 1150 – c. 1230' (died in Acre); Sefaria 1150-1230 (both approximate); the paper's text 'בסביבות 1230' (its own reference list titles the National Library entry 1150-1214). The row keeps כ־1150–1230 (birth 1150 in every source, death hedged), and the bio now says only 'the first half of the 13th century' and names both dates with their sources (the first version stated 'around 1230' flatly). THE ALIYAH: the first version said that in 1209-1211 he stood at the head of the aliyah; the dates and the co-leader Rabbi Yehonatan of Lunel are the paper's alone, while en.wikipedia and Sefaria say he joined the 300 rabbis who emigrated about 1211 and he.wikipedia calls him one of the heads of the aliyah, so the bio says 'around 1211, as one of the leaders'; the paper's 1209-1211 and Yehonatan (278) stay in the colleague link, which rests on the paper. THE YESHIVA: the paper says he founded a famous yeshiva in Sens; en.wikipedia says he took charge of the yeshiva of Sens after the Ri's death; he.wikipedia only says he settled in Sens; the bio says he headed a well-known yeshiva there. 'EDITED' the Tosafot of Sens was replaced by 'wrote' (he.wikipedia: מחבר תוספות שאנץ; the Chida: שחיבר). The core idea: 'brought to its peak the dialectical approach of the study house of Rashi, Rabbenu Tam and Ri' is the paper's evaluation (Rashi was not his teacher), now attributed; the Jerusalem Talmud and Tosefta claim is en.wikipedia's (the paper's 'most French and Ashkenazi sages focused almost exclusively on the Bavli' is not repeated); the Rosh's remark is in Sefaria (Responsa of the Rosh, rule 84) and the paper ('Ri' = Ri HaZaken and 'R. Shimshon' = the Rash: Sefaria says so). Birthplace: unknown (he.wikipedia), probably Falaise (en.wikipedia, Urbach), so the bio says France. Shem HaGedolim: Maarekhet Sefarim Tav 19:21 (under 'Tosafot') says that the Tosafot of Sens were written by 'Rabbenu Shimshon bar Avraham of Sens, a student of the Ri' and that Rabbenu Eliezer of Touques abridged them; the earlier null is replaced. Place: Sens coordinates 48.1972, 3.2833 as read from Wikipedia's API (coords.json). Links: all from the sources' statements on this sage (teachers Rabbenu Tam 33, the Ri 275; elder brother the Ritzba 279; students Yitzchak of Corbeil 303 (he.wikipedia, en.wikipedia) and Moshe of Coucy 588 (paper)); NEW colleague 278 (paper). Not linked: Meir HaLevi Abulafia (293: lively correspondence then a quarrel; no link type fits cleanly), Rosh (598, an evaluation), Yaakov of Corson (not on the roster). Left out: the burial (Haifa tradition vs Acre/Carmel), the Sifra commentary (disputed attribution), the Kitav al-Rasa'il exchange.
